title: Assessment of RNPOs, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
outcomes: Apply registration rules for non-profit organisations.
Compute application and accumulation of income.
Tax specified income, anonymous donations and accreted income.
Apply provisions for political parties, electoral trusts and private trusts.
Apply pass-through rules for business trusts, investment funds and securitisation trusts.

meta.exam_tip: For RNPOs, compute regular income, then 85% application, then accumulation and specified income.

concepts.title: Registration of non-profit organisations
body: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, charitable and religious trusts and institutions are "registered non-profit organisations" (RNPOs). Registration under section 332 is granted by the PCIT/CIT; new entities first get provisional registration (valid three years), and regular registration is valid for five years, renewable on application within the specified time.

Charitable purpose (section 2(23)) includes relief of the poor, education, yoga, medical relief, preservation of environment and monuments, and other objects of general public utility — the last subject to limits on receipts from trade, commerce or business.
Before granting registration, the authority examines the genuineness of activities and compliance with other laws; registration can be cancelled for specified violations under section 351.
concepts.analogy: Registration is the gateway to exemption.
concepts.work: A new school trust gets provisional registration before commencing activities.

concepts.title: Application and accumulation of income
body: An RNPO must apply at least 85% of its regular income to its objects in India during the year (section 341). Amounts applied from corpus, loans or borrowings are not application when spent, but reinvestment into corpus or repayment of the loan within five years counts then. Donations to another RNPO count only at 85% of the amount given; corpus donations to another RNPO are not application.

Section 343 deems 15% of regular income accumulated. Any further unapplied income can be accumulated under section 342 for up to five years by stating the purpose in a statement filed before the return due date, and investing in permitted modes (section 350). Unutilised or misused accumulation becomes taxable.
Expenditure paid in cash above ₹10,000 per day, TDS defaults (30% disallowed) and capital expenditure claimed twice are not treated as application.
concepts.analogy: Spend 85%, park 15%, and formally accumulate the rest.
concepts.work: Applying ₹38 lakh out of ₹50 lakh leaves ₹4.5 lakh to accumulate under section 342.

concepts.title: Specified income, anonymous donations and violations
body: Specified income of an RNPO — such as income not applied or accumulated, income on violation of conditions, and benefits to related persons — is taxed at 30% (section 334).

Anonymous donations above the higher of 5% of total donations and ₹1,00,000 are taxed at 30%, except for wholly religious trusts (fully exempt) and religious-cum-charitable trusts (taxed only on anonymous donations earmarked for educational or medical purposes).

Specified violations under section 351 — application for non-objects, business beyond limits, false claims, non-compliance with other laws — can lead to cancellation of registration. On cancellation, merger with a non-RNPO or dissolution, accreted income (assets less liabilities at FMV) is taxed at the maximum marginal rate under section 352 ("exit tax").
concepts.analogy: Breaking the rules costs exemption and can trigger exit tax.
concepts.work: Anonymous donations of ₹6 lakh out of ₹50 lakh total leave ₹3.5 lakh taxable at 30%.

concepts.title: Political parties, electoral trusts and private trusts
body: A political party holding registration under section 29A of the 1951 election law is exempt (section 12 with Schedule VIII) on house property, capital gains, other sources and voluntary contributions, if they keep books, record contributions above ₹20,000, get accounts audited, accept no donation above ₹2,000 other than by banking channels, submit the contribution report to the Election Commission and file the return.
Electoral trusts are exempt on voluntary contributions if they distribute at least 95% of contributions received during the year to registered political parties.

Private discretionary trusts are taxed at the maximum marginal rate on their entire income, except where beneficiaries have no other taxable income above the exemption limit, for the only trust declared by will, for specified pre-1970 trusts for dependants, and for employee welfare funds — which are taxed as an AOP. Oral trusts are taxed at the maximum marginal rate (section 308).
concepts.analogy: Parties must keep records; private discretionary trusts face top rates.
concepts.work: Rent earned by a compliant political party is exempt.

concepts.title: Business trusts, investment funds and securitisation trusts
body: Business trusts (REITs and InvITs) under section 223: interest and dividend from the SPV and rental income of a REIT pass through to unit holders, who are taxed on those components; the trust is taxed on other income, mainly capital gains, at applicable rates. Distributions as repayment of debt are treated as income of the unit holder in specified cases.

Investment funds (Category I and II AIFs) under section 224: income other than business income passes through to unit holders and is taxed as if earned directly; business income is taxed in the fund's hands at the applicable rate.
Securitisation trusts under section 221: income is exempt in the trust and taxed in the investors' hands as if they had invested directly, with TDS by the trust.
concepts.work: Rent earned by a REIT is taxed in unit holders' hands, not the REIT's.

illustrations.title: Shortfall in application
illustrations.q: Seva Sankalp Foundation, a registered NPO, has regular income of ₹50,00,000 for T.Y. 2026-27 and applies ₹38,00,000 to its objects in India. Compute the amount it must accumulate under section 342 to avoid tax, and the tax if it does not.

illustrations.title: Anonymous donations
illustrations.q: Prakash Vidya Trust, a registered educational NPO, receives total donations of ₹50,00,000 in T.Y. 2026-27, including anonymous donations of ₹6,00,000. Compute the tax on anonymous donations.

checks.label: Exclusion: higher of 5% of total donations and ₹1 lakh (₹)

jobs.title: Year-end compliance for an NPO
jobs.situation: A trust has unspent funds and anonymous donations at year-end.
steps: File accumulation statement for any balance.
Confirm registration validity and filing dates.
jobs.takeaway: Missing a statement can turn surplus into taxable income.

summary: Specified income and anonymous donations at 30%.
Political parties Schedule VIII; electoral trusts 95%.
remember: Anonymous donation exclusion: higher of 5% and ₹1 lakh.
traps: Treating corpus donations to another RNPO as application.

viva.q: Are anonymous donations to a wholly religious trust taxed?
viva.model: They are fully exempt for a wholly religious trust.

viva.q: When is spending from a loan treated as application?
viva.model: It counts in the year the loan is repaid out of income, provided this happens within five years.
The aggregate fair market value of assets less liabilities of the RNPO on the specified date, taxed at the maximum marginal rate.

viva.q: How is a private discretionary trust taxed?
viva.model: At the maximum marginal rate on its whole income, subject to specified exceptions taxed as an AOP.

viva.q: How is business income of a Category I or II AIF taxed?
viva.model: In the hands of the fund; other income passes through to unit holders.

It maintains books, gets them audited, files its contribution report and return on time, but accepted one cash donation of ₹5,000.
